previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient, a woman with T1-T2 paraplegia and chronic obstructive lung disease, was readmitted 48 hours after discharge due to worsening dyspnea, hypoxia, and green secretions. She was found to have hospital-acquired pneumonia caused by Pseudomonas aeruginosa, confirmed by sputum culture, and was treated with intravenous antibiotics including meropenem, later transitioned to ertapenem for outpatient completion. She required ICU-level care initially for sepsis with hypotension, which resolved with fluids and pressors. A PICC line was placed to facilitate home antibiotic therapy. Her COPD exacerbation was managed with nebulizers, suctioning, and a short course of prednisone. She stabilized, was weaned to home oxygen, and discharged with home health services and follow-up plans.

Brief Hospital Course:
Ms. ___ is a ___ woman with T1-T2 paraplegia, COPD, multiple 
recent admissions for pneumonia, who was admitted to the MICU 
with hypoxia and altered mental status found on vital signs at 
___ clinic. After being on pressors for about 24hrs, she 
stabilized and was transferred to the regular medicine floor on 
___.
.  
ACTIVE ISSUES:
.
#. Hypoxia: The patient was found to be significantly hypoxic in 
the ED.  Her exam, CXR, leukocytosis, and increased sputum 
initially suggested pneumonia and she was started on 
broad-spectrum antibiotics.  She was treated with vancomycin 
given coag + staph on prelim sputum Cx, ciprofloxacin for 
empiric pseudomonal coverage, and meropenem for UTI (see below). 
She was given nebulisers, and her O2 sats remained in the high 
80's on ___ NC. Her oxygen requirements stabilized over the 
course of her MICU stay and she was transferred to the regular 
medicine floor on ___ with vitals Temp 98.8F, BP 92/56, HR 80, 
R 24, O2-sat 98% 4L.
.
On the medicine floor, the pt was feeling better and did not c/o 
SOB. She occasionally desatted to the 80's when feeling anxious 
and tearful, but otherwise remained in the 90's on 2L NC. She 
was initially continued on vancomycin, meropenem, and 
ciprofloxacin. Given persisting hypoxia since admission, CTA 
chest ___ was ordered which showed no evidence of pulonary 
embolism, and a left lower lobe consolidation and small 
effusion, likely representing PNA (less likely atelectasis). She 
had several ABG's showing normal pH but pCO2 in the 70's; the pt 
also had high bicarb which is likely robust compensation for 
chronic respiratory acidosis. On ___, pt was stable with 
further resolving SOB and improved lung sounds on exam, satting 
98% on 2.5L NC.
.  
#. Sepsis: The patient was hypotensive in the ED, even relative 
to her home BP's which are already low.  The initial concern was 
for sepsis versus hypovolemia.  She was fluid responsive but did 
require levophed, which was weaned after about 24 hours in the 
MICU, after which her SBP remained in the 90's (her normal 
baseline). On the medical floor, pt remained hemodynamically 
stable.
.  
#. Altered mental status: She had repeated episodes of 
somnolence and difficulty being aroused.  However, these appear 
to be a chronic issue and precede the current episode of hypoxia 
and hypotension.  The cause is unclear, but her numerous 
medications for pain and anxiety may be contributing to her 
underlying hypercarbia and infection.  By the time of discharge, 
the pt's mental status was AAOx3 and mentating well without 
confusion.
.  
#. UTI: The patient has a history of recurrent UTIs in the 
setting of straight cathing.  Past cultures have grown ESBL 
organisms, including Klebsiella sensitive only to meropenem.  
Her urine culture on this admission grew the same, and so she 
was treated with meropenem. She was transitioned to ertapenem 
for outpatient antibiotic administration.
.  
#. PNA: The patient may have had some component of hypercarbia 
in setting of COPD and sedating medications at home.  She was 
continued on her home albuterol and ipratropium. Her sputum 
prelim grew out coag + staph. She was treated with vancomycin as 
above.
.  
INACTIVE ISSUES:
.
#. Depression: Reportedly increased from baseline despite home 
celexa. Patient was previously amenable to seeing a psychologist 
as an outpatient.  
.  
#. T1-T2 paraplegia with chronic pain: The patient had 
maintained on multiple medications at home including baclofen, 
clonazepam, lidocaine patch, methadone, oxybutynin, pregabalin, 
trazodone, oxycodone.  Several of these medications were  
temporarily discontinued in the hospital given concern for 
sedation (oxycodone, clonazepam, trazodone).  
.  
#. Hypothyroidism - TSH was 0.64. The patient was continued on 
her home levothyroxine.
.

PICC PLACEMENT

INDICATION:  Paraplegic patient with urinary tract infection.

OPERATORS:  Drs. ___ (fellow), ___ (resident)
and ___ (attending physician).

PROCEDURE:  Patient was placed supine on the imaging table in the
interventional suite.  Procedure was explained to the patient.  Timeout was
performed as per ___ protocol.

Under aseptic conditions and sonographic guidance, a micropuncture needle was
placed in the right basilic vein.  Sonographic images were printed prior to
and following needle placement and are on file.  A 0.018 wire was passed via
the needle into the IVC.  Needle was exchanged over the wire with a peel-away
sheath. Appropriate measurements were made.  Inner dilator was removed.  A 41
cm 4 ___ single-lumen Power PICC was placed over the wire with its tip in
the lower SVC.  Wire was removed.  Sheath was peeled away.  Catheter was
secured to the skin by a StatLock.  Appropriate dressing was applied.  Patient
tolerated the procedure well and no immediate post-procedure complications
were seen.

FINDINGS:
1.  Access site at right brachial vein.
2.  PICC tip in the lower SVC.

IMPRESSION:  Uncomplicated placement of a 41 cm 4 ___ single-lumen PICC in
the right brachial vein with its tip in the lower SVC with ultrasound and
fluoro guidance.

CT CHEST WITHOUT AND WITH IV CONTRAST

CLINICAL HISTORY:  Evaluate for pulmonary embolism or pneumonia.  Please also
comment about azygoesophageal recess mass and reactive lymphadenopathy
previously described.

FINDINGS:

Initial non-contrast evaluation demonstrates a left-sided IJ central venous
catheter to be present, with the tip noted to be in the left brachiocephalic
vein.  Right-sided central venous catheter appears to be a PICC, terminating
in the mid-to-lower SVC.

Bilateral shoulder hardware is present, and changes are seen related to prior
right-sided posterior rib fractures as well as a left-sided fractures are
post-surgical change as well.

After the IV administration of contrast, there is no evidence of pulmonary
embolism.  

There are predominantly atelectatic changes at the left lower lobe, and a
milder component at the dependent aspect of the right lung base, although
slight hypoenhancement in this region suggests that superimposed pneumonia is
considered.  Examination of lung windows demonstrates some debris within the
dependent aspects of the trachea, series 4, image 6.  This raises the
possibility of aspiration as a cause of this atelectasis +/- consolidation. 
Note is made of an azygous fissure.  

Note is made of some collapse of the trachea and central airways on the first
non-contrast examination compared to the contrast-enhanced examination, which
may represent changes of tracheobronchomalacia.

The lobulated structure in the right paravertebral region adjacent to the
azygoesophageal recess and just posterior to the right atrium appears
essentially unchanged in size.  Although the morphology is slightly different,
current measurement is approximately 2.7 x 2.3 cm, while a comparable
measurement from the prior examination would be 2.5 x 2.3 cm.  

However, some of the right hilar adenopathy, which was present on the prior
examination has improved, with no significant hilar adenopathy evident on
today's examination.  There is no mediastinal or axillary lymphadenopathy
evident.  Small lymph nodes in the AP window measure approximately 6 mm in
size, and a lymph node at the left pulmonary artery trunk origin measures 11
mm.  These appear essentially unchanged.  

Limited visualization of upper abdominal structures is grossly unremarkable.

IMPRESSION:

1.  No evidence of pulmonary embolism.

2.  Atelectatic changes at both lung bases, with some hypoenhancements
suggesting some degree of superimposed infection as well.  In the presence of
tracheal secretions, aspiration is a consideration.

3.  Unchanged appearance of the right paravertebral soft tissue mass adjacent
to the azygoesophageal recess and posterior to the left atrium.

4.  Right hilar lymphadenopathy has decreased since the prior examination.

5.  Left-sided internal jugular vein catheter tip is in the region of the left
brachiocephalic vein.
